title: Why everyone has a belly button
examples: Why do we have belly buttons?
What is a belly button for?
Why do some people have an outie belly button?

nodes.label: Umbilical cord
nodes.ask: What does the umbilical cord do?

explain.say: Before you were born, you could not eat or breathe. Everything you needed came through a tube joined to your tummy: the umbilical cord.

draw.text: Why everyone has a belly button

nodes.label: Umbilical cord
nodes.ask: What does the umbilical cord do?

explain.say: The cord connects the baby to the placenta, an organ that grows on the wall of the womb. There, food and oxygen pass from the mother's blood into the baby's blood, without the two bloods mixing.

nodes.label: Umbilical cord
nodes.ask: What does the umbilical cord do?

explain.say: The cord carries this rich blood to the baby and takes waste such as carbon dioxide back to the placenta. It enters the body exactly where your belly button is now.

nodes.label: Umbilical cord
nodes.ask: What does the umbilical cord do?

explain.say: After birth the baby can breathe and feed, so the cord is clamped and cut, which does not hurt. The small stump dries and drops off in one to two weeks, and the scar that is left is your belly button.

stages.note: No nerves in the cord, so it does not hurt

stages.label: Stump dries
stages.note: It shrivels over a few days

stages.label: Stump drops off
stages.note: Usually within one to two weeks

stages.label: Belly button

faq.q: What does the umbilical cord do?
faq.a: The umbilical cord is a tube with blood vessels that joins an unborn baby to the placenta. It brings food and oxygen to the baby and carries waste away.
asks: How does a baby eat before it is born?

faq.a: The placenta is an organ that grows in the womb during pregnancy. The mother's and baby's blood flow very close together there, so food and oxygen can pass across while the two bloods stay separate.
asks: How does a baby breathe in the womb?

faq.q: Does cutting the umbilical cord hurt?
faq.a: No. The umbilical cord has no nerves, so neither the baby nor the mother feels it being clamped and cut.
asks: Does it hurt the baby when the cord is cut?
Why is the cord cut after birth?

faq.q: How long does the cord stump take to fall off?
faq.a: The small stump left after the cord is cut dries out and usually falls off by itself within one to two weeks, leaving the belly button.
asks: When does the cord stump fall off?
What happens to the umbilical cord after birth?

faq.q: Why do some people have an outie belly button?
faq.a: Whether you have an innie or an outie depends mostly on how the skin and scar tissue healed after the stump fell off, not on how the cord was cut. Most people have innies.
asks: What makes an innie or outie?
Is an outie belly button normal?

facts: The belly button, or navel, is the scar left where the umbilical cord was attached.
The umbilical cord usually contains two arteries and one vein.
In the placenta the mother's and baby's blood do not normally mix.
